newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: IMF to give Philippines clean bill of health.
newsitem.headline: IMF to give Philippines clean bill of health.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund team visiting the country for a review would give the Philippines good marks when it leaves later this week, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo told a news conference on Wednesday.
"They're about to leave here giving us a clean bill of health and a lot of strong statements our economy is in good shape," De Ocampo told reporters.
"The IMF feels our growth rate is in good shape, including the current account gap which is four percent of GNP which they continue to find reasonable," he said.
He said the Philippines surpassed almost all the performance criteria in the first quarter such as public sector borrowing, base money, net international reserves and levels of external financing.
The IMF was however concerned about delays in the passing of the comprehensive tax reform package.
Congress has said it expects to pass this bill into law by October.
De Ocampo said the non-passage of the bill had prompted the government to scale down its budget surplus this year to 7.1 billion pesos from 13 billion pesos.
The Philippines will end its three-year programme with the IMF this year when it passes the tax package.
